subject: Production streaming: intermittent stalls and high tail latency

Cc: support@quantumpay.com, Daniel Park <daniel.park@quantumpay.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 22:18:00 -0700
Subject: Production streaming: intermittent stalls and high tail latency

Hi Logan —

We started seeing intermittent stalls yesterday evening in our customer-facing chat widget. Messages will stream for a few tokens and then hang for 6–20s before resuming. This affects about 3–7% of sessions and spikes during checkout flows. Attachments: client_trace_qpay_0511.json and a short log snippet (streaming_latency_debug_20270511.log).

What we've tried so far:
- Retrying at the client (exponential backoff) recovers but yields a poor UX.
- Reducing max_tokens in the request slightly reduced the incidence but did not eliminate it.

Can you confirm if there was any capacity event or known change to streaming endpoints in us-west-2 on May 11? We need a short-term mitigation we can push tonight.

Thanks —
Alice
Alice Cho
SRE, QuantumPay
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Production streaming: intermittent stalls and high tail latency

Hi Alice — thanks for the quick heads up and for the traces. We're treating this as an incident and our on-call infra team is investigating now. Immediate suggestions you can apply client-side that often reduce user-facing impact:

1) Graceful fallback: if streaming stalls > 3s, switch to a short non-streaming completion request (same model) to get the remainder of the response while continuing to capture the streaming request id for server-side debugging.
2) Token window: temporarily set max_tokens to 200 for chat turns that historically spike.
3) Retry & dedupe: implement a 2x retry with jitter and tag requests with a client-generated id to dedupe server-side.

We're collecting more logs; I'll loop you back with a summary and an ETA for a remediation. Apologies for the disruption — we know this pattern hurts checkout UX.

— Logan
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Production streaming: intermittent stalls and high tail latency

Logan / Alice — short tech update from infra on-call after initial triage:

- Root cause hypothesis (high level): a combination of autoscaler oscillation on a subset of GPU pools in us-west-2 + suboptimal batching heuristic for very short streaming turns (avg seq length < 64) created transient kernel-selection thrash. That thrash causes a KV-cache missstorm that blocks token emission for ~5–18s in affected processes.
- Evidence: correlated spikes in kernel-selection time and per-process KV evictions; we see a cluster of latency anomalies at 2027-05-11T21:50–23:30Z that align with your traces.

Immediate mitigations we've deployed (rolled to a limited set of hosts now):
A) Pinning: temporarily pin your routing policy to a stable model variant (redwood/gpt-mini-stable) which uses a more conservative kernel path.
B) Batching tweak: reduce batching window for streaming lanes to 8ms to avoid accumulating incompatible request shapes.
C) KV cache sizing: increase per-process KV cache by 25% for the next 12 hours in the us-west-2 pool.

Short-term trade-offs: a small increase in cost per token for pinned traffic and slightly lower throughput on the pinned variant. We prioritized user-facing latency.

Next steps (engineering):
- Today: observe pinned routing and batching tweak for 24 hours and verify tail latency falls below 1s 99th.
- 72h: deploy kernel-selection fallback so kernel thrash auto-detects and falls back to the stable execution path.
- 14 days: iterate on batching heuristics to better separate very-short and long-turn traffic.

I've attached a short timeline and the initial log slice (streaming_latency_debug_20270511.log). We'll continue to update this thread.

— Monica
Monica Patel
SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Production streaming: intermittent stalls and high tail latency

Alice / Daniel — quick summary of what we just deployed and recommended actions for QuantumPay: 

What we did (rolled 23:00–00:30 UTC):
- Pinned your routing for streaming chat to redwood/gpt-mini-stable in us-west-2 for traffic tagged with account=qpay-prod.
- Reduced batching window for streaming lanes to 8ms in the affected pool.
- Increased per-process KV cache size by 25% for the pool.

Client-side mitigations we recommend pushing tonight (low effort):
- Implement a short-circuit: if no bytes arrive on the stream for 3 seconds, call the non-streaming /completions endpoint with same prompt and client_request_id; merge the returned content into the UI when available.
- Add a lightweight UI spinner and a soft reconnect message so users know we’re recovering the reply.
- Keep the client-generated id header (X-Client-Req-Id) to help us dedupe.

Expected outcome: we expect 99th-percentile token emission latency to return below 1s for pinned traffic within 2 hours of the change. We will monitor and share a 24h tail-latency graph.

Can we schedule a 30-minute sync today (14:00 PT) to review data and next steps? If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite and a short incident summary doc.

Thanks for the quick collaboration — we take this seriously.

— Logan
